newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Peso fall makes Philippine business lower output.
newsitem.headline: Peso fall makes Philippine business lower output.

text.p: Philippine industries are reducing output for the holiday season due to the sharp depreciation of the peso, Federation of Philippine Industries president Raul Concepcion said in a statement on Monday.
"With the rapid deterioration of the peso and with interest rates very high, business and industry are at a standstill," he said.
The peso fell to a record low of 30.24 to dollar in afternoon deals on Monday, a 14.5 percent drop since its effectivate devaluation on July 11.
"Based on a preliminary flash survey of manufacturers, their foremost concern is to be liquid. Domestic manufacturers are scaling down their production for the holiday season," he said.
"They are concerned that consumers will reduce their spending for postponable goods. On the other hand, manufacturers are also concerned that they may be caught with a high replacement cost."
Concepcion said he was calling a meeting of industry and business leaders this week to exchange views on how they have been coping with the present uncertainty.
